channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Copper: Prices supported by tightening stocks – ING
item.description: ING’s Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey report that Copper prices edged higher on progress in US-Iran talks, which eased transit and inflation concerns. They note that falling SHFE and LME inventories underpin fundamentals, while Chinese refined Copper output rose in May on better smelter margins.

item.title: Canadian Dollar falls back against US Dollar ahead of US flash PMI data
item.description: The Canadian Dollar (CAD) retreats against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday after a short-lived pullback move the previous day.

item.title: Oil: US-Iran progress weighs on prices – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank reports that diplomatic progress in US-Iran talks has pressured Oil, with Brent falling to USD 77.90 and WTI also lower. A 60‑day US license allows Iran to sell crude internationally, and more than 30 million barrels have already departed for Asia.

item.title: United States Dollar Index hovers around 101.00 ahead of US PMI data
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which measures the value of the US Dollar (USD) against six major currencies, holds gains near a 13-month high of 101.13, reached on June 19, during the early European hours on Tuesday. Traders await S&P Global US Purchasing Managers Index (PMI) data due later in the day.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar stays resilient ahead of key PMI data
item.description: Here is what you need to know on Tuesday, June 23:

item.title: Japanese Yen: Downside bias as BoJ lags Fed – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Michael Wan notes that the US Dollar (USD) is edging stronger, with USD/JPY moving closer to 162.00 as Asian currencies weaken in an orderly fashion. He highlights a sharp intraday move in the Japanese Yen (JPY) and possible policy discussions between US and Japanese officials.

item.title: WTI slumps below $73.00 as traders continue to watch US-Iran peace talks
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI), the US crude oil benchmark, is trading around $72.75 during the early European trading hours on Tuesday. The WTI price falls to the lowest level since early March as traders continue to watch US-Iran moves.

item.title: Gold falls to $4,100 neighborhood on resilient USD, Fed hike bets and Iran uncertainty
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) extends its steady intraday descent through the early European session on Tuesday, with bears now eyeing the $4,100 mark amid a broadly firmer US Dollar (USD). Despite positive signals from US-Iran peace talks, investors remain skeptical over a final deal.

item.title: Indian Rupee struggles for direction amid firm US Dollar, lower oil prices
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) opens on a flat note against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday.

item.title: NZD/USD Price Forecast: Kiwi tests YTD lows at 0.5683 in cautious markets
item.description: The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) extends losses against the US Dollar (USD) for the fifth consecutive day on Tuesday, reaching levels sub-0.5700, and approaching year-to date lows, at 0.5683.

item.title: Euro: Rate spread pressure EUR against US Dollar – Danske Bank
item.description: Danske Research Team notes that EUR/USD started the week under pressure as widening interest rate differentials favor the US Dollar over the Euro.

item.title: AUD/USD Price Forecast: Tests descending channel bottom around 0.6950
item.description: AUD/USD continues its losing streak for the sixth consecutive day, trading around 0.6960 during the Asian hours on Tuesday. The technical analysis of the daily chart shows the pair remaining within the descending channel pattern, suggesting a prevailing bearish bias.

item.title: GBP/USD Price Forecast: Bearish bias persists as pair tests Symmetrical Triangle breakdown zone
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) trades slightly lower against its major currency peers during the European trading session on Tuesday, but remains firm against Asia-Pacific currencies.

item.title: British Pound: Range trading with downside risk against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that GBP/USD closed little changed at 1.3250 after intraday swings, leaving momentum broadly flat and favoring near-term range trading between 1.3205 and 1.3275.

item.title: Euro: Services PMI reaction in focus – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Michael Pfister highlights persistent headwinds for the Euro after dovish comments from European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde reduced market expectations to roughly 33 basis points of further tightening this year.

item.title: Japan’s core CPI, excluding special factors, climbs 2.7% in May vs. 2.8% rise in April
item.description: The Bank of Japan (BoJ) said on Tuesday that Japan's core consumer inflation rate excluding one-off factors, as measured by the Japanese central bank's new gauge, climbed 2.7% in May. This figure exceeded the BoJ’s 2% target and eased from 2.8% in April.

item.title: Euro declines below 1.1450 on US-Iran peace deal uncertainty, traders await Eurozone, US PMI data
item.description: The EUR/USD pair trades with mild losses around 1.1425 during the early European session on Tuesday. The US Dollar (USD) edges higher against the Euro (EUR) amid risk-off sentiment and a hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) stance.

item.title: USD/JPY Price Forecast: Holds above 161.50; eyes multi-decade top despite intervention fears
item.description: The USD/JPY pair enters a bullish consolidation phase during the Asian session on Tuesday and currently trades just above 161.50 amid mixed fundamental cues.

item.title: India's HSBC Manufacturing PMI eases in June: What 54.5 means for the Indian Rupee
item.description: The preliminary reading of India's HSBC Manufacturing Purchasing Managers Index (PMI) eases to 54.5 in June versus 55.0 prior, the latest data published by S&P Global and HSBC Bank showed on Tuesday.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah declines as MSCI downgrade risks loom
item.description: USD/IDR extends its gains for the second consecutive day, trading around 17,900 during the Asian hours on Tuesday. Meanwhile, severe economic headwinds are building for Southeast Asia's largest economy.

item.title: India Gold price today: Gold falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Gold prices fell in India on Tuesday, according to data compiled by FXStreet.

item.title: Asia stocks decline on Iran risks; South Korea’s KOSPI slumps 6%
item.description: Most Asian equity markets fell on Tuesday, tracking the overnight slump in US technology stocks, prompting investors to take profits following a powerful artificial intelligence-driven rally.

item.title: AUD/JPY Price Forecast: Holds losses below 113.00 on intervention fears, bias stays mildly bullish
item.description: The AUD/JPY cross trades in negative territory around 112.75 during the early European trading hours on Tuesday. The Japanese Yen (JPY) strengthens against the Australian Dollar (AUD) as traders are on high alert for currency intervention from Japanese authorities.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD falls to near $63.00 as bearish bias persists
item.description: XAG/USD depreciates over 3% after registering modest gains in the previous day, trading around $63.20 per troy ounce during the Asian hours on Monday.

item.title: Swiss Franc holds onto losses below 0.8100 amid firm Fed interest rate hike bets
item.description: The Swiss Franc (CHF) holds onto Monday’s losses around 0.8088 against the US Dollar (USD) during the Asian trading session on Tuesday.

item.title: Australian Dollar falls despite improved S&P Global PMI data
item.description: AUD/USD extends its losses for the sixth consecutive day, trading around 0.6980 during the Asian hours on Tuesday. The pair remains subdued despite the release of improved preliminary Australian S&P Global Purchasing Managers Index (PMI) data.

item.title: 101: United States Dollar Index remains close to 13-month highs
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which measures the value of the US Dollar (USD) against six major currencies, remains steady after registering modest gains in the previous day and is hovering around 101.00 during the Asian hours on Tuesday.

item.title: New Zealand softens to near 0.5700 despite US-Iran peace progress
item.description: The NZD/USD pair trades in negative territory for the fifth consecutive day around 0.5705 during the Asian trading hours on Tuesday. The US Dollar (USD) strengthens against the New Zealand Dollar (NZD) on a hawkish tone from the US Federal Reserve (Fed).

item.title: Japan’s Kihara says will take appropriate action against FX moves if needed
item.description: Japan’s Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara said that he will take appropriate action against the foreign exchang (FX) moves if needed, Reuters reported on Tuesday.

item.title: Canadian Dollar hangs near April 2025 lows vs USD amid bearish oil, BoC-Fed divergence
item.description: The USD/CAD pair attracts some dip-buyers following the previous day's modest pullback from its highest level since April 2025 and trades around the 1.4165-1.4170 region during the Asian session on Tuesday.
